Issued at 120 PM CDT Thu Oct 22 2026

Tonight - Saturday: Abnormal Warmth Continues; Low Precipitation 
Potential

Upper level ridging and anomalously high 500hPa heights remain 
situated across much of the central United States through at 
least Saturday while southerly flow and weak warm air advection 
continue under said ridge resulting in 850hPa temperatures 
around 10-14C. Given these warm temperatures aloft, continue to 
expect abnormal warmth as we head into the weekend, roughly 15 
to 20 degrees above normal.

Upper level troughing begins to move across the United 
States/Canada border tonight, phasing with a shortwave that 
ejects off a cutoff low across the southwest United States. 
Surface cyclogenesis occurs over the northern Great Plains on 
Friday as a result, leading to a developing 850hPa low level jet
from Nebraska into northern Minnesota Friday afternoon. Given 
the proximity of the LLJ to our area along with some weak 
700-500hPa PVA associated with the shortwave, can't rule out a 
few light showers/sprinkles for our northern counties Friday 
afternoon as suggested by several of the CAMs. However, the vast
majority of the region is expected to remain dry as soundings 
depict dry air below 10kft where the strongest forcing will 
occur and rather weak forcing within the saturated upper 
portions of the atmosphere. Current probabilities for light 
showers/sprinkles only sit around 10%. 

As the upper level trough and attendant surface low continue 
eastward Saturday, the cold front associated with these features
slows down and becomes quasi-stationary across Minnesota into 
northern Wisconsin. Moisture pools along the boundary as 
southerly flow continues across the region which combined with 
forcing along the front and stronger 700-500hPa PVA should lead 
to some precipitation development throughout the day Saturday. 
However, because the boundary largely remains to our west, most 
of the region is again expected to be dry with only those north 
and west of an Austin, MN to Wausau, WI line having 10-20% 
probabilities to see some light rain.

Sunday - Wednesday: Greater Precipitation Potential, Trending Cooler

The quasi-stationary boundary slowly sags southward throughout 
the day Sunday though moisture begins to become more limited 
with time and forcing becomes far more nebulous as this feature 
becomes separated from its upper level support. While some light
showers are possible Sunday mainly for those north of I-90, 
probabilities have come down slightly, sitting around 10-20% in 
the 22.13z NBM though as high as 30-40% per the AIFS Ens and 
AIGEFS. Regardless, amounts should remain under 0.1". 

Greater precipitation potential exists Monday through Tuesday 
as the cutoff low across the Desert Southwest begins to lift 
northward. How this feature evolves as it moves northward and 
where the heaviest rainfall associated with it will occur 
remains rather uncertain though. The GEFS/AIGEFS members largely
suggest the low takes a more southern trajectory, keeping 
higher probabilities for precipitation across a majority of the 
Upper Mississippi River Valley (60-80%) whereas the EPS/AIFS Ens
on the other hand suggest a more northern and western solution,
keeping higher probabilities across Minnesota into northern 
Wisconsin. Given the uncertainty, probabilities for 
precipitation remain on the lower end, currently sitting around 
30-40% in the 22.13z NBM though these probabilities may 
increase as the models begin to converge on a solution. 

Other than precipitation potential, the passage of the quasi- 
stationary front on Sunday will allow cooler temperatures to 
begin filtering into the Upper Midwest. There is a great deal of
spread within the 25th-75th and 10th-90th percentiles of the 
ensemble guidance related to the temperature forecast Monday 
through Wednesday however, around 10 and 20 degrees 
respectively, due in no small part to the different scenarios 
mentioned above. That said, the overall trend is towards more 
seasonable temperatures through the beginning of the new week.
